subject.title: [Bug]: read tool drops memory/ prefix in multi-agent setup, causing ENOENT

question: Should maintainers accept https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96453's guarded bare-date read fallback as the fix for this issue, or require the fix to stay upstream in startup/prompt path handling?
rationale: The bug is real-looking and source-backed, but the candidate fix changes generic read fallback semantics and depends on preserving sandbox validation before synthesized filesystem access.

options.title: Accept the guarded fallback
options.body: Land the linked PR if maintainers agree that an ENOENT-only `YYYY-MM-DD.md` to `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` retry is the right compatibility fix.

options.title: Require prefix preservation upstream
options.body: Ask for a revised fix in the startup or prompt path if maintainers do not want the read tool to infer daily-memory paths.

options.title: Keep issue open without the PR
options.body: Close or reject the linked PR only if maintainers want a different owner boundary while preserving this issue as the canonical bug.

recommendation.title: Accept the guarded fallback
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR if maintainers agree that an ENOENT-only `YYYY-MM-DD.md` to `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` retry is the right compatibility fix.

likelyOwner.reason: The pending decision centers on the agent read-tool boundary and workspace sandbox validation, where Vincent Koc has recent adjacent merged work.
